environment.description: ECS Fargate service with container filesystem configured as chroot jail under /srv/jail with bind-mounted read-only /app directory. The task definition specifies a custom process namespace with 'pidMode: task' and the container runs with a read-only root filesystem (readonlyRootFilesystem: true). The chroot jail directory /srv/jail contains only the application code and a synthetic tokens.db with randomized dummy entries regenerated every 30 seconds by a sidecar container. The API_SECRET_KEY environment variable is populated from a Secrets Manager reference that rotates every 60 seconds via a Lambda rotation function, meaning any timing-derived partial key information becomes invalid before enough characters can be recovered. Additionally, the ECS service is placed behind a CloudFront distribution with Origin Shield enabled in the same region, introducing variable CDN-layer buffering (response coalescing) that adds 2-50ms of non-deterministic latency per request, destroying sub-millisecond timing signal fidelity required for the character-by-character attack.

config.secrets_rotation: AWS Secrets Manager with 60-second Lambda rotation for API_SECRET_KEY
config.sidecar: token-regenerator container rewrites /app/data/tokens.db every 30s with random values
config.cdn: CloudFront with Origin Shield (same-region), response buffering enabled
config.network_path: Client -> CloudFront Edge -> Origin Shield -> ALB -> Fargate task
